demand_analysis.distribution_type: Mixed/Bimodal — high-volume working days interspersed with near-zero or zero demand days

lead_time_analysis.stability: Moderate — mostly sub-day deliveries with periodic spikes to 3–4 days

safety_lead_time.comparison_action: INCREASE — SAP safety lead time is 0.0 days; recommend setting to 1.40 days to buffer against observed lead time variability (CV=0.78)

narrative: Material PL3__MCBEE8AD exhibits a bimodal demand pattern: most working days carry ~2,500–3,000 units of throughput, while a minority of days record near-zero or zero demand, yielding a CV of 0.43. Lead times are short on average (1.09 days) but volatile (CV=0.78), with occasional spikes to ~3.9 days that drive the safety stock requirement. The chosen (r,Q) policy with EOQ-based order quantity of 9,352 units replaces the current near-daily MOQ-driven replenishment cadence with ~73 annual orders, cutting ordering costs by ~92% while only modestly increasing holding costs, for a net saving of ~$47,275 per year.
warnings: Storage capacity nearly binding: safety_stock (3798) + order_quantity (9352) = 13150 units vs max_storage_units (13794.6). Utilization = 95.3%. Minor demand or lead time spike could breach capacity.
Unconstrained EOQ (9699 units) was capped to 9352 units to respect max_storage_units constraint.
SAP safety lead time is 0 days; data evidence supports setting it to 1.40 days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: High daily throughput (~2,546 units/day), moderate demand CV (0.43), and short but volatile lead times make a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs; the reorder point embeds a statistically derived safety stock at the 95th percentile of lead-time demand. The policy is simpler to implement in SAP than (s,S) and avoids the over-ordering induced by the current MOQ-only setup.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The EOQ order quantity is capacity-constrained (unconstrained EOQ=9,699 vs cap=9,352). Post-replenishment inventory reaches 95.3% of max_storage_units. Any positive demand shock during the review period or a delayed delivery could push on-hand stock above capacity if a second order arrives early. Recommend reviewing warehouse allocation or negotiating a marginal storage extension.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility. MOQ (714) + safety_stock (3,798) = 4,512 < 13,795. Feasible. However, near-capacity utilisation (95.3%) warrants a supply-chain review of storage allocation for this material.
